# US Consumer Sentiment Falls as Inflation Expectations Rise

The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index fell to 47.8 in early September 2026, down for a second consecutive month and well below market expectations of 51.0, according to the preliminary estimate.

It was the weakest reading since May’s record low.

## University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for September 2026 Declines 7.5% Month-Over-Month, Year-ahead Inflation Expectations Rise to 4.6%. Sentiment Under Trump is Down
results.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Preliminary Results for September 2026 Declines 7.5% Month-Over-Month, Year-ahead Inflation Expectations Rise to 4.6%. Sentiment Under Trump is Down 13.2% Year-Over-Year and 32% Lower Than Biden in September 2024.

Shoppers at an outlet mall in Concord, North Carolina.

Consumer sentiment has dropped in September, according to the initial reading of the University of Michigan’s monthly survey.

The survey’s index stands at 47.8, versus the 51.7 recorded at the end of August. Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a reading of 51.4.
